description: An additive voice after the Crumar GDS: nothing is filtered away, the output is a sum of up to sixty-four sine partials, and every control says how something varies from the first partial to the last

params.text: Tilts the levels across the partials, which is the slope of the spectrum
Balances the odd-numbered partials against the even-numbered ones
Stretches the partials away from whole-number multiples the way a real string's do, so the upper ones run sharp
Spreads the partials across the stereo pair: clockwise fans them outward in order and anticlockwise scatters them
Sets where between the quiet and loud spectra the tone is drawn from, which velocity is added to
Spreads the envelope rates across the partials, so the high ones die sooner than the low ones
Spreads the envelope start times across the partials, so the tone blooms upward, or the highs speak first and the fundamental builds underneath
Sets how long each partial takes to reach full level, read in milliseconds
Sets how long each partial takes to fall to the sustain level, read in milliseconds
Sets the level each partial holds at while the gate is high
Sets how long each partial takes to fall away after the gate drops, read in milliseconds
Spreads that oscillator's effect across the partials, from the low ones to the high ones
Sets the frequency above which partials are dropped from the sum; it removes partials rather than filtering the output
Emphasises the partials near the cutoff rather than resonating a filter

inputs.text: Sets the pitch as a volt per octave; the number of channels here is what sets the polyphony, up to sixteen voices
A rise starts a note on that channel and a fall releases it
Sets how hard each note is struck, which crossfades the tone between the quiet and loud spectra rather than only making it quieter
Changes the spectral slope, added to the tilt knob
Changes the odd and even balance, added to that knob
Changes the inharmonicity, added to the stretch knob
Changes the stereo spread, added to the width knob
Changes where between the two spectra the tone is drawn from, added to the morph knob
Changes the spread of envelope rates, added to that knob
Changes the spread of envelope start times, added to that knob
Moves the cutoff a volt per octave, added to the cutoff knob
A rise restarts that oscillator's phase
Changes the emphasis near the cutoff, added to the resonance knob

outputs.text: The left side of the summed partials
The right side of the summed partials

notes: the module holds two complete spectra, one for a quiet note and one for a loud one, and velocity crossfades between them, so a quiet note is a different timbre
the per-partial levels, detunes, envelope depths and rates, and the modulation matrix, are all edited on the display, which cannot be reached by clicking for help
the three oscillators' depths, delays and randomness, and the velocity response settings, have no knob on the panel and are reached from the menu
menu: Preset — a submenu of twenty-one settings, each one chosen to exercise a different part of the engine rather than to be a sound
Partials: 16, 32, 64 — sets how many sine partials are summed, which trades detail against how much work the module does
Voice allocation: First available, Rolling — chooses whether a new note takes the first free voice or the next one in turn
PITCH tab snaps to: Free, Cents, Semitones, Octaves — sets what a drag on the per-partial detune display produces; the value is stored in cents either way
Touch response — a submenu setting how far velocity moves the level, where that range falls, and how far it moves the timbre
LFO delay and random — a submenu setting each oscillator's delay and randomness; randomness also frees each voice's phase, so the voices drift apart rather than locking together
Reset spectrum — returns the per-partial levels, detunes and envelopes to their starting values
Reset modulation — empties the modulation matrix
